note: Bluff-top state beach campground strung along Carlsbad Blvd for nearly 2 miles above the open Pacific, with stairways down to the sand. The oceanfront premium sites line the bluff edge; only 8 of the sites have hookups (two standard and six oceanfront doubles). Very popular, especially in summer. The entrance is reached northbound only: from Poinsettia Ln continue north on Carlsbad Blvd and U-turn at Breakwater Rd. --Claude

flags: WATERFRONT: stored 'bayview' -> recommend 'coastal walk'. This is the open Pacific, not a bay (the CA brief keeps bayfront/bayview for SF/Humboldt/Tomales/Morro/Mission bays). The camp lies between Carlsbad Blvd and the bluff edge, with nothing between the west-row pads and the beach but the bluff face, and parks.ca.gov says 'Stairs lead to the beach' - an easy walk to the ocean with no highway, town or day-use complex in between (Carlsbad Blvd and the town are on the inland side). An on-water value is ruled out: the pads are on an ~18 m bluff (3DEP: camp 21 m, beach 2-3 m, 40-70 m west of the profile start 33.1040,-117.3196), a climb-down. Oceanfront premium sites per ReserveCalifornia include #1, #60, #170 and the doubles #215-222; the Esri frame at 33.1040,-117.3200 shows the bluff-edge row. Replacement evidence: 'parks.ca.gov "Stairs lead to the beach" + Esri 2026-11-27: pads in a strip between Carlsbad Blvd and the bluff edge, only the ~18 m bluff face (3DEP) between the west row and the beach; open Pacific, no highway/town/day-use between -> coastal walk (bluff rules out on-water)'.
